devices.title: Other devices
devices.body: Things this bridge reaches over the network rather than by infrared: other SLWF units, WLED and ESPHome devices, a computer to wake, a sensor to read. Once added they appear on the control page and can be used in automations.
devices.name: What to call it
devices.token: API token, if it needs one
automations.title: Automations
automations.body: Rules that run on this device, whether or not anything is watching. Each one says: if these things are true, then do these things.
learn.press_button_to_bind: Press the button you want to use, on any remote.
learn.bind_failed: That button could not be saved.
learn.bind_is_ac_remote: That is a button from the air conditioner's own remote. The bridge needs those to follow what the unit is doing — please pick a button from a different handset.
remotes.title: Use another remote
remotes.body: The bridge hears every remote in the room, not just the air conditioner's. Pick a button you never use on your TV handset — a colour key, teletext, a spare input — and make it control the air conditioner.
remotes.label: What to call it
remotes.warning: Do not use a button from the air conditioner's own remote — the bridge needs those to follow what the unit is doing, and it will tell you if you try.
control.hold_pending: Starting as soon as the compressor may restart
control.not_configured_body: The bridge does not know how to talk to your unit. Teach it with your remote — it usually takes one button press.
learn.press_any_button: Point your air-conditioner remote at the bridge and press any button.
learn.did_it_react: I recognised the protocol and sent that command straight back. Did the air conditioner react — a beep, a display change, anything?
learn.not_recognised: I heard the remote clearly but cannot rebuild its commands from scratch. I can try every protocol I know, or record your buttons one at a time.
learn.set_remote_to: Set your remote to this, then press its send button:
learn.recording_complete: All codes recorded. Your air conditioner is ready.
learn.protocol_adopted: Protocol adopted. The bridge can now build any command by itself.
learn.try_sweep_or_record: That protocol was not it. Try sweeping every protocol, or record raw codes.
learn.sweep_watch: Watch the air conditioner. I am sending a test command with each protocol in turn.
learn.sweep_exhausted: None of the known protocols worked. Recording raw codes is the way forward.
learn.timeout: Nothing happened for five minutes, so I stopped waiting.
teach.title: Teach the bridge your remote
teach.intro: Start with Identify. One button press is usually enough: if the protocol is recognised, the bridge can then build every command by itself, including combinations you never demonstrated.
teach.record_modes: Which modes should I record? (comma separated, e.g. cool,heat)
teach.overflow_body: the frame was longer than the capture buffer
teach.nothing_body: press a button on your remote
teach.manual_body: If you already know your unit's protocol, choose it here and skip learning entirely.
teach.test_sent: Test command sent — did the unit react?
teach.db_body: Profiles contributed by other owners. Importing one configures the bridge without any learning at all.
teach.db_offline: Could not reach the database — this needs internet access.
teach.submit_body: Once your AC works, export the profile and open a pull request so the next owner of the same model does not have to teach anything.
teach.no_codes: No raw codes stored — the protocol is doing the work.
clients.title: Who may control it, and who is told
clients.body: Every client speaks to the same internal API — most both send commands and receive the state. Switching one off here blocks it without disturbing the others.
mqtt.homie: Also publish the Homie convention (openHAB, Domoticz)
webhook.title: Webhook
webhook.body: Sends the new state to a URL of yours every time the air conditioner changes, whoever changed it. Anything that can receive a request can follow along — Node-RED, a script, a logger.
webhook.http_only: Plain http:// only — a second encrypted connection does not fit on this device. Point it at something on your own network.
webhook.sent: Test sent — check the receiving end
modbus.title: Modbus TCP
modbus.body: For building-management systems and PLCs. Exposes the air conditioner as plain holding registers.
other.title: Other ways in
other.body: Endpoints for software that already speaks something else. Switched off until you want them: a way in nobody uses is a door nobody asked for.
telegram.open: Let the next person to message become the owner
telegram.hint: Create a bot with @BotFather, paste its token here, then send /start to your bot from the phone that should control the air conditioner.
uart.events: Emit state changes as JSON lines
uart.warning: UART0 is shared with the serial console. Enabling this stops log output on the port so the protocol framing stays clean.
network.title: Wi-Fi
network.connecting: Connecting — the device may change address.
security.title: Access control
security.hint: The token lets scripts and integrations call the API without a browser login — send it as Authorization: Bearer …
scenes.title: Scenes
scenes.body: One-tap presets. A scene only changes what you put in it, so a "Quiet" scene can set just the fan speed and leave everything else alone. Scenes appear on the control page, in Telegram, and as a dropdown in Home Assistant.
stats.title: Usage
stats.energy_note: Energy is running time multiplied by the rated power you entered — good enough to spot trends, but it is an estimate, not a meter.
teach.min_off_hint: Minimum off time protects the compressor: after the unit switches off, a request to start it again waits out the remaining seconds instead of short-cycling it. Rated power is only used for the energy estimate — leave it at 0 if you do not know it.
schedules.title: Schedules and timers
schedules.no_clock: The clock has not synchronised yet — schedules will not fire.
system.title: Device
system.name: Friendly name
system.pins_hint: Defaults follow the SLWF-12 r1.0 schematic: the receiver module (J2) sits on GPIO4 and the emitter driver (Q3) on GPIO16. Change these only if your board differs.
system.update_hint: Upload firmware.bin to update the program, or littlefs.bin to update this interface.
system.factory_confirm: Erase every setting and learned code?
clock.unsynced: The device does not know what time it is
clock.pick_first: Choose a date and time first
clock.now_body: Schedules, timers and time-based automations all read this clock. The board has no battery, so it starts each time from nothing and asks a time server on the internet.
clock.zone_body: Sets what the device calls 8 o'clock, including when summer time starts and ends. Worth getting right even without a time server.
clock.manual_body: For a device with no way out to the internet. The time you set holds until the device restarts — there is no battery to keep it — and a time server, if one ever answers, takes over.
clock.geo_ok: Location filled in — save to keep it
clock.no_geo: This browser will not say where it is
clock.geo_body: Only used to work out sunrise and sunset, on the device and with no network at all. Rules can then say “half an hour before sunset”, which keeps meaning the same thing all year — a fixed hour does not. Leave it blank and the sun is simply not mentioned.
lang.title: Language
lang.body: English is built into the device and always available. Other languages are files that can be added — once added, a language stays on the device and works with no internet at all.
lang.not_a_pack: That file is not a language pack
lang.more_body: The device never contacts anything on its own. If you ask, this browser — not the device — will fetch the list of available languages from the project's page on GitHub, and then the one you pick. The pack is sent to the device over your own network and kept there.
lang.look_ask: This browser will now connect to GitHub to fetch the list of available languages. The device itself will not connect to anything. Continue?
lang.all_here: Every available language is already installed.
lang.file_body: For a browser that cannot reach GitHub either — on the device's own setup network, for instance. Download the pack on any machine and choose the file here. Nothing leaves your network.
locale.title: Localisation
locale.formats_body: How this device writes things down, and which unit it speaks to the air conditioner in. The unit is not only a display choice: it goes out in the infrared frame, so the unit's own display follows it.
clock.ntp_body: Empty, and the device asks nobody: the browser sets the clock the first time it opens this page, which is enough for a device that has somebody looking at it now and then. Name a server and the device will keep itself synchronised instead — useful if it runs untouched for months.
clock.ntp_hint: none — the browser sets the clock

teach.no_protocols: Could not load the protocol list
teach.emitter_sent: Blinking for a second and a half — point a phone camera at the front of the box. Use the selfie camera: most rear cameras filter infrared out.
